initiatives.name: Accelerating Growth Plan (AGP) — Restaurant Exit
initiatives.summary: Whitbread aims to reach 96,000 open rooms in the UK and Ireland by 2030/31 (including AGP extension rooms), with a long-term potential of 125,000 rooms, driven by new builds, conversions, extensions and single-site acquisitions.

evidence.title: Extension of Accelerating Growth Plan to exit all branded restaurants
evidence.summary: Whitbread is proposing to extend its Accelerating Growth Plan (AGP) to replace all 197 remaining branded restaurants with an integrated F&B offer, converting them into higher-returning hotel extension rooms. This is part of a pivot to become a pure-play budget hotel business, subject to employee consultation.
evidence.quote: In 2026/27, we plan to move to a single, integrated F&B offer, which is tailored specifically for the needs of the Premier Inn guest, across all of our sites as we exit all of our remaining branded restaurants.

evidence.title: Sale of branded restaurants (51 completed, 60 agreed)
evidence.summary: Whitbread completed the sale of 51 branded restaurant sites for £50m as part of its AGP, with a further 60 sites having agreed terms of sale subject to conditions, enabling capital recycling into higher-returning hotel extension rooms.
evidence.quote: having concluded the sale of 51 branded restaurants for £50m, with a further 60 sites where we have agreed terms of sale subject to conditions, we are now proposing to reallocate capital and extend the previous plan

evidence.title: UK network expansion to 125,000 room long-term potential
evidence.summary: Whitbread aims to reach 96,000 open rooms in the UK and Ireland by 2030/31 (including AGP extension rooms), with a long-term potential of 125,000 rooms, driven by new builds, conversions, extensions and single-site acquisitions.
evidence.quote: Assuming sites can be secured at the right price, over the longer term, we have the potential to reach 125,000 open rooms, which is 45% more than we have open today.

evidence.title: Accelerating Growth Plan strategic transformation
evidence.summary: Whitbread references an ongoing 'Accelerating Growth Plan' as a strategic transformation program affecting its business, including reduced purchases of high-carbon food and overall operational restructuring. The company plans to fully update its Scope 3 emissions baseline once the programme completes in 2027/28.
evidence.quote: Because our Accelerating Growth Plan is still underway, we will update our Scope 3 baseline fully once we complete the programme in 2027/28.

initiatives.name: Five-Year Plan for £300m Incremental Profit
initiatives.summary: Whitbread plans to recycle at least £1bn of its more mature property assets to fund future growth and drive higher financial returns, taking advantage of a more favorable property investment market outlook.

evidence.title: Issuance of new £400m bond
evidence.summary: Whitbread successfully completed the issuance of a new £400 million bond in February 2025, maintaining a strong balance sheet reflected by its investment grade rating.
evidence.quote: We successfully completed the issuance of a new £400m bond in February 2025 and our balance sheet remains strong, as reflected by our investment grade rating.

evidence.title: Five-Year Plan to drive £300m incremental profit
evidence.summary: Whitbread announced a Five-Year Plan in October 2024 targeting at least £300m incremental adjusted profit before tax and more than £2bn for share buy-backs and dividends by 2029/30. The plan includes recycling at least £1bn of mature property assets and is built around three strategic pillars: UK growth, German expansion, and capability enhancement.
evidence.quote: Given our strong balance sheet and our confidence in the delivery of our Five-Year Plan, that includes recycling at least £1bn of our most mature property, we expect to generate at least £300m of incremental profit and more than £2bn for share buy-backs and dividends by 2029/30.

evidence.title: Average net capex of £500m per annum through 2029/30
evidence.summary: Whitbread plans to maintain average net capital expenditure of £500m per annum through to 2029/30 to support growth across the UK and Germany while increasing return on capital, supported by a strong balance sheet.
evidence.quote: Maintaining average net capex at £500m per annum Our strong balance sheet and prudent investment approach means we can continue to invest in growing our business whilst also increasing our return on capital.

evidence.title: Recycling £1bn of mature property assets
evidence.summary: Whitbread plans to recycle at least £1bn of its more mature property assets to fund future growth and drive higher financial returns, taking advantage of a more favorable property investment market outlook.
evidence.quote: With a more favourable outlook in the property investment market, we will look to recycle at least £1bn of our more mature property assets to fund future growth and drive higher financial returns.

evidence.title: £250m share buy-back programme
evidence.summary: Whitbread is accelerating shareholder returns with a £250m share buy-back to be completed over the next twelve months, reflecting confidence in the Five-Year Plan and balance sheet strength.
evidence.quote: Given our confidence in our Five-Year Plan, together with the strength of our balance sheet, we are recommending a final dividend of 60.6p per share and are accelerating the planned delivery of shareholder returns with a £250m share buy-back to be completed over the next twelve months.

initiatives.name: Food Distribution Logistics Restructuring
initiatives.summary: Whitbread moved to a new procurement model using a shared logistics service for the majority of food and consumables distribution, replacing a previously leased delivery fleet. The new model is described as more efficient both financially and from a carbon perspective, reducing Scope 1 and Scope 3 Category 3 emissions.

evidence.title: Shift to shared logistics service for food distribution
evidence.summary: Whitbread moved to a new procurement model using a shared logistics service for the majority of food and consumables distribution, replacing a previously leased delivery fleet. The new model is described as more efficient both financially and from a carbon perspective, reducing Scope 1 and Scope 3 Category 3 emissions.
evidence.quote: The key structural change in our 2025/26 Scope 3 relates to the inclusion of emissions from a shared logistics service for the majority of food and consumables within Category 4 (Upstream transportation and distribution). Previously, emissions from this activity were reported under Scope 1, as the delivery fleet was leased by the Group. As the new procurement model is more efficient, both financially and from a carbon perspective, emissions reported in Category 3 (Fuel‑ and energy‑related activities) decreased by 34%.
